exercises.title: Four steady pulses on C
instructions: Find the key sending MIDI note 60 (middle C).
Count aloud 1-2-3-4 and play one note per beat with either hand.
Leave small, comfortable space between notes. Repeat three times; pause if tense.
exercises.self_check: Can you play three four-note passes at an even pulse without discomfort?

exercises.title: Eight even subdivisions
instructions: Use C4 / MIDI note 60.
Count 1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and. Play one note per count.
Do not accelerate during the second half; retain relaxed release.
exercises.self_check: Were the eight attacks evenly spaced at the chosen tempo?

exercises.title: Five-key stepwise motion
instructions: Locate consecutive white keys C-D-E-F-G.
Move upward and back down, one note per click, separately with either hand.
Keep the motion light; fingering can be chosen to fit your comfort.
exercises.self_check: Can you repeat the direction changes cleanly and comfortably?

exercises.title: Small keyboard skips
instructions: Locate C-D-E-F-G.
Play C-E, D-F, E-G as six separate notes, one per beat.
Aim for accurate landings without looking down at every motion.
exercises.self_check: Were the interval skips accurate without a strained wrist?

exercises.title: Soft and strong on one note
instructions: Play MIDI note 60 six times on an even beat.
Alternate soft and a moderately stronger attack, avoiding harsh or forced motion.
Listen for contrast before examining MIDI velocity readings.
exercises.self_check: Could you hear three soft-strong pairs without tension?

exercises.title: Dynamics across a small phrase
instructions: Play C-D-E-F-G-F-E-D, one note per beat.
Alternate softer and stronger attacks while keeping pitch and time stable.
Treat the contrast as phrasing, not a force or speed test.
exercises.self_check: Did the expression remain deliberate across the moving notes?

exercises.title: Read and locate five staff notes
instructions: Export or display the five-note score and name each note aloud before playing.
Play one note per beat, checking both staff position and key location.
Do not infer reading skill from MIDI note matching alone.
exercises.self_check: Could you identify each written note before playing without simply memorizing the finger pattern?

exercises.title: Read sharps and flats in short phrases
instructions: Read the printed accidentals (C C# D Eb E F E Eb D C# C).
Name each altered note, locate the key, then play slowly.
Repeat without forcing speed; correct visual reading matters more than the MIDI match.
exercises.self_check: Did you read each sharp/flat rather than guessing from the sound or neighboring key?

exercises.title: Alternate left and right in steady time
instructions: Use the left hand for the lower notes C3 D3 E3 F3, then the right hand for C4 D4 E4 F4.
Alternate hands, one note per beat, with no extra gap at hand changes.
A MIDI recording cannot prove which hand you used; self-check explicitly.
exercises.self_check: Were your hands coordinated with an even pulse and minimal tension?

exercises.title: Hands-together chord and melody preparation
instructions: Practice left-hand C3 E3 G3 C3 and right-hand C4 E4 G4 C4 separately first.
Then play matched octave pairs together as a separate musical-context task.
Use self-report/recording, not the sequential MIDI gate, to assess simultaneity.
exercises.self_check: Did both hands begin the octave pairs together without one hand dragging?

exercises.title: Circle of fourths root navigation
instructions: Say the roots C F Bb Eb Ab Db Gb B E A D G C.
Locate each target note deliberately; stay in comfortable keyboard range.
Name each interval before looking at any diagram.
exercises.self_check: Could you name and locate the next fourth without reading a memorized list?

exercises.title: Circle of fifths reverse traversal
instructions: Say C G D A E B F# Db Ab Eb Bb F C, observing enharmonic names.
Play roots slowly, without assuming all notes are natural.
Connect adjacent roots to key signatures, not only finger motion.
exercises.self_check: Could you reverse direction and explain the sharp/flat key relationship?

exercises.title: Major and minor triad construction
instructions: Build C-E-G, then A-C-E as separate arpeggios.
Identify the 4+3 and 3+4 semitone stacks before playing.
Play as block triads only after you can name the notes.
exercises.self_check: Could you describe why one triad is major and the other minor?

exercises.title: Triad inversions and voice-leading
instructions: Construct C major root, first inversion, second inversion in a comfortable register.
Play each voicing as an arpeggio before playing as a block.
Notice shared tones and minimize movement; MIDI does not assess fingering or voice leading.
exercises.self_check: Could you identify root, first, and second inversion by lowest chord tone?

exercises.title: A natural minor and the key signature
instructions: Name each note of A natural minor, comparing it to C major.
Play A-B-C-D-E-F-G-A slowly, then describe its relative major.
Use the score rather than relying solely on your memorized sequence.
exercises.self_check: Could you identify the half-step locations and explain the relative major?

exercises.title: A harmonic minor and raised seventh
instructions: Contrast A natural minor G with harmonic minor G#.
Read and play the raised seventh, then resolve it to A.
Mark the sharp on your score rather than changing the key signature.
exercises.self_check: Could you correctly identify and play the raised seventh accidental?

exercises.title: Build seventh chords from stacked thirds
instructions: Build Cmaj7 (C E G B) and Am7 (A C E G).
Arpeggiate each before playing as a full four-note chord.
Describe root, third, fifth, seventh and the difference in chord quality.
exercises.self_check: Could you identify each chord tone and play both chords comfortably?

exercises.title: Four-note chord inversions and smooth movement
instructions: Compare Cmaj7 root position with its first inversion E G B C.
Practice arpeggiated and block voicings slowly; record finger comfort.
Pay attention to hand span; do not stretch through discomfort.
exercises.self_check: Did you move between voicings smoothly while identifying the inversion?
